issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. Only the test SMILES are featurized. No test labels, files or network are used, and all randomness comes from the seed (seed + i).
No bug that would make the result meaningless. The median over 6 XGB members, (6, n_test) stacked along axis=0, returns one prediction per test molecule.

Recomputed z from one run on each side: diff = 0.3828 - 0.3795 = 0.0033. The sd of the difference is 0.0037*sqrt(2) ≈ 0.00523, so z ≈ 0.63. This matches the harness's 0.635; the small gap is rounding. The gain is within noise, so reject is the right call unless a replicate confirms it.

Minor: the comment says each member costs 'roughly the same', but n_est*depth only roughly matches tree cost. The ensemble fits about 3900 trees against the incumbent's 600, so the job takes about 6.5x longer. It is unlikely to hit the 10-minute limit, but it adds complexity for a gain within noise.
